diagnosis.observed: Exact f75 browser evidence shows the initial tail reached real ProductionRenderer. Ten failures each have exactly one initial getHumanConversationTranscriptTail(limit=200) request and zero older beforeSeq requests; all eleven renderer-errors attachments are empty. Failure precedes the ten cases' intended later behavior assertions.
diagnosis.classification: Production readiness propagation defect plus a test setup assumption that an automatic initial older-page probe must occur before any user scroll. Source-backed causal diagnosis; no browser instrumentation directly traced the effect callback.
production_causal_chain: Fixture renders the actual ProductionRenderer. openAlice clicks Alice and awaits visible m3, then expects older pending=1 without a scroll.
openAgent retrieves the initial Human transcript tail; fixture returns m3/m4/m5 and nextBeforeSeq=3 with nextBeforeCursor=fixture-human-walk:3.
ProductionRenderer installs that cursor into the real pagination controller and subscribes to its snapshot.
At f75, snapshot.hasOlder is true for both unprobed and more. loadOlder returns without any request unless cursor.kind is more.
ConversationTranscript's near-top effect depends on hasOlder/isLoadingOlder/olderLoadFailed/loadOlder, installs a scroll listener, and immediately calls maybeLoadOlder. loadOlder callback is stable.

An initial effect at unprobed can therefore perform a no-op; the later unprobed-to-more update does not change hasOlder and does not itself rerun that effect. No scroll is performed in original openAlice, so increasing wait time does not provide a missing trigger.

When genuinely at the top, the production fix changes the view readiness from false to true once a usable cursor arrives; the effect can then rerun while keeping unprobed/exhausted distinctions inside the controller.

diagnosis.environment_claim: No evidence supports classifying these ten errors as runner/network/browser-install failure. Browser loaded actual renderer, compile and prior16 dialog tests passed; page-error attachments are empty.
diagnosis.fixture_repair_limit: e4's helper dispatches scroll on the real viewport after eight requestAnimationFrame ticks, keeping 11 cases and cursor/row assertions. That exercises explicit user-scroll history loading, but the frame count is not a proof of cursor readiness, and manual scrolling alone can bypass the production auto-probe defect.
diagnosis.stale_comment: e4 helper comment says unprobed->more keeps hasOlder=true. This remains true of the controller snapshot API but no longer of the view handoff after parent441; interpret as historical fixture reasoning, not as current production-prop behavior.
diagnosis.minimal_action: Do not duplicate the existing repair or extend timeouts. Retain the one-line readiness handoff repair and all behavioral assertions. Read terminal exact-H runs for 441 (production fix with original no-scroll spec) and e4/current descendant (both fixes) before claiming the common failure is resolved. If no-scroll coverage remains invalid due to intended initial bottom-positioning, keep explicit-scroll cases and separately qualify the intended automatic near-top readiness contract; do not lower the gate.
